claims.text: A post-deposition heat treatment at approximately 900°C will induce nano-sized intermetallic precipitates in the FeNiCrCoCu coating matrix.
Nano-sized intermetallic precipitates impede dislocation motion in the FeNiCrCoCu matrix.
Impeded dislocation motion reduces microscopic plastic deformation under high-temperature sliding stresses.
Reduced plastic deformation caused by precipitate barriers reduces coating wear.
Heat-treated FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have lower wear rates than untreated coatings during sliding at 700–900°C.
Heat-treated FeNiCrCoCu coatings will show less cross-sectional plastic deformation than untreated coatings during sliding at 700–900°C.
The predicted comparison assumes comparable normal loads and sliding speeds.
The beneficial precipitate effect is expected to apply in the approximately 700–900°C sliding regime.
At temperatures notably above the stated regime, the beneficial effect may weaken or disappear.
At lower temperatures, the precipitates may not form effectively and the beneficial effect may weaken.
Long-term high-temperature exposure may alter precipitate stability and consequently alter wear improvements.
